description: Harvest every valid 2x2 DID comparison from a staggered panel and aggregate them via precision-weighted / simple / cohort-weighted averages. Agnostic to cohort structure; useful for robustness comparisons against CS / SA / BJS. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: a paper-standard estimator is the target -- harvest_did is a robustness comparison against CS / SA, not a replacement for them. Cost: Number of harvested 2x2 comparisons grows as cohorts x periods squared. Assumptions: Parallel trends hold for every valid 2x2 sub-comparison being harvested and aggregated; No anticipation before each cohort's first treated period (reference horizon -1 is clean); Independence across units (unit-level influence functions; the joint covariance across cells, horizons and estimated weights is propagated). Pre-conditions: Long-format panel with unit, time, outcome columns; Either a binary treat indicator or a precomputed cohort (first-treatment) column with a never_value marker; Multiple cohorts and overlapping periods so valid 2x2 comparisons exist across the requested horizons. Failure modes: No clean (never-treated or not-yet-treated) controls so no valid 2x2 cells can be...

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

horizons.description: Event-time horizons to evaluate. Defaults to ``[-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4]``. Positive values are post-treatment, ``0`` is the first treated period, negative values are placebo/pre-trend.

never_value.description: Value that marks "never treated" in the ``cohort`` column. If you use ``treat``, units without any treated observation are mapped to this value automatically.

reference.description: Pre-treatment reference horizon relative to each cohort

weighting.description: How the harvested 2x2 estimates are aggregated: 'precision' inverse-variance (minimum-variance under independence), 'equal' unweighted, 'n_treated' by each comparison's treated-unit count.

name: harvest_did

description: Hausman specification test between two fitted models: one consistent under both hypotheses (IV, fixed effects), one efficient under the null (OLS, random effects). Compares the coefficients they share with a generalised inverse of V_b - V_B; degrees of freedom are its rank. sigmamore=True bases both covariances on the efficient model's variance, the form to use for IV against OLS (Stata hausman, sigmamore). Not valid with robust or clustered covariances: use sp.estat(iv, 'endogenous') or sp.xtoverid instead. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Assumptions: Both estimators are consistent under the null and the second is efficient there; The difference of the two covariance matrices is positive semi-definite; with robust or clustered covariances it need not be, and the statistic is then not chi-squared; Both models are fitted on the same sample with the same coefficient names.

alpha.description: Level of the decision

sigmaless.description: Use the consistent model's disturbance variance for both

sigmamore.description: Use the efficient model's disturbance variance for both

name: hausman

description: Hausman test for FE vs RE in panel data. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Assumptions: The fitted model whose result is passed in is correctly specified for the test in question; Wald tests use that fit's variance estimator (robust / clustered if it was), so inference inherits its validity; Hausman: the efficient estimator is efficient under the null, and the difference of covariance matrices is positive definite. Pre-conditions: A fitted StatsPAI result object (sp.regress / sp.logit / ...) -- these functions do not take raw data. Failure modes: Hausman statistic negative / covariance difference not positive definite -> Use the regression-based (auxiliary) Hausman test or a robust version; a negative statistic is evidence for the null. Alternatives: sp.sp.margins, sp.sp.test, sp.sp.regress.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

sigmamore.description: Stata's ``hausman fe re, sigmamore``: both covariance matrices use the RE disturbance variance. Use it when the classical statistic is negative (``recommendation == "inconclusive"``).

name: hausman_test

description: reghdfe-style OLS with high-dimensional fixed effects. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: vce='conley' on more than ~20,000 rows -- dense O(n^2) memory (see cost); use sp.conley on the fitted result instead. Cost: Absorption is linear in n. vce='conley' is the exception: the within-transformed design goes through conley_vcov_matrix, which builds dense n x n distance and kernel matrices -- ~80 GB at n=100,000. vce='cr2'/'cr3' are per-cluster and cheap by comparison. Assumptions: Linear conditional mean after absorbing high-dimensional fixed effects (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell); Exogeneity of regressors conditional on the absorbed fixed-effect dimensions; Clustered SEs require enough clusters for asymptotics; multiway cluster needs each dimension well-populated. Pre-conditions: Continuous outcome; Fixed-effect factor variable(s) in the '| fe1 + fe2' part of the formula. Failure modes: Singleton groups absorb their own observations and bias clustered SEs -> Keep drop_singletons=True so singletons are removed before estimation; Alternating-projections absorber does not converge -> Raise maxiter / loosen tol, or reduce the number of FE dimensions; Too few clusters make wi...

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

cluster.description: One-way or multi-way cluster column(s).

conley_cutoff.description: Conley distance cutoff in km for ``vce="conley"``.

conley_lag.description: Panel Conley: spatial + time HAC as Stata ``acreg ..., id() time() lag()`` with ``pfe1() pfe2()``. Pairs within a unit take the time kernel alone up to ``conley_lag`` periods; pairs of different units take the spatial kernel times the time kernel up to ``conley_lag_cross`` periods (``acreg``'s ``lagdist()``, default 0: contemporaneous only). All three must be given together. Without them the spatial kernel runs over every pair of rows, which on a panel treats a unit's own rows in different periods -- and every cross-period pair of neighbours -- as correlated; that warns.

conley_lag_cross.description: Time bandwidth for pairs of different units (``lagdist()``).

conley_time.description: Panel Conley: spatial + time HAC as Stata ``acreg ..., id() time() lag()`` with ``pfe1() pfe2()``. Pairs within a unit take the time kernel alone up to ``conley_lag`` periods; pairs of different units take the spatial kernel times the time kernel up to ``conley_lag_cross`` periods (``acreg``'s ``lagdist()``, default 0: contemporaneous only). All three must be given together. Without them the spatial kernel runs over every pair of rows, which on a panel treats a unit's own rows in different periods -- and every cross-period pair of neighbours -- as correlated; that warns.

conley_time_kernel.description: Time kernel of the panel variant (``acreg``'s ``hac`` is Bartlett, ``1 - |dt| / (lag + 1)``; without ``hac`` it is uniform).

conley_unit.description: Panel Conley: spatial + time HAC as Stata ``acreg ..., id() time() lag()`` with ``pfe1() pfe2()``. Pairs within a unit take the time kernel alone up to ``conley_lag`` periods; pairs of different units take the spatial kernel times the time kernel up to ``conley_lag_cross`` periods (``acreg``'s ``lagdist()``, default 0: contemporaneous only). All three must be given together. Without them the spatial kernel runs over every pair of rows, which on a panel treats a unit's own rows in different periods -- and every cross-period pair of neighbours -- as correlated; that warns.

df_inference.description: Reference distribution of the p-values and confidence intervals. ``None`` (default) follows ``reghdfe``'s ``e(df_r)``: ``t(G - 1)`` under clustering (``G`` = the smallest cluster count, capped at the residual df), ``t(N - K - df_a)`` otherwise. ``'resid'`` uses the residual df also under clustering (StatsPAI <= 1.32, close to the normal with many observations); ``'normal'`` the standard normal; a number that many degrees of freedom. The standard errors are the same in every case.

formula.description: ``"y ~ x1 + x2 | fe1 + fe2 + fe3"``. The ``| fe...`` part is optional. Both sides accept bare names, ``c.x`` / ``i.f``, ``a:b``, ``a*b``, ``f1^f2`` and the varying-slope forms ``i.f#c.x`` / ``i.f##c.x`` / ``f[[x]]`` / ``f[x]`` -- see the module docstring for the full grammar. Any Python identifier is a column name, so non-ASCII names (`` ~ ``) work. A third part makes it 2SLS, Stata's ``ivreghdfe``: ``"y ~ exog | fe1 + fe2 | endog ~ z1 + z2"`` (``"y ~ 1 | ..."`` without exogenous regressors). All variables are swept of the fixed effects by the same absorber, then 2SLS runs on the residuals; ``cluster=`` (one way), ``vce='robust'`` or iid SEs follow ``ivreg2``'s small-sample conventions, and ``result.iv_diagnostics`` carries the first-stage F tests, Kleibergen-Paap rk LM and Wald F, Cragg-Donald F, Anderson-Rubin test and Hansen J (all as ``ivreghdfe ..., first``).

se_type.description: Override automatic inference of SE type. Usually inferred from ``cluster`` / ``wild``.

tol.description: Convergence tolerance of the absorber (largest change of a sweep, relative to the variable's scale). Default ``1e-8``, or ``1e-12`` when a varying slope (``i.f#c.x`` / ``f[x]``) is absorbed: slope sweeps converge slowly, and at ``1e-8`` the SEs of a four-FE model with a quarter-specific slope were still 1e-5 away from reghdfe's (which converges at its own 1e-8), against 4e-8 at ``1e-12``. reghdfe's collinearity screen is derived from ``1e-8`` either way.

vce.description: Canonical SE-menu keyword (matches ``sp.regress`` / ``sp.feols``): - ``"robust"`` / ``"hc1"`` -- heteroskedasticity-robust on the FE-absorbed design with reghdfe's small-sample factor ``N/(N-k-df_a)``; matches Stata ``reghdfe ..., vce(robust)``. - ``"hc0"`` -- no small-sample factor. - ``"CR2"`` / ``"CR3"`` / ``"jackknife"`` -- Pustejovsky-Tipton (2018) bias-reduced cluster-robust on the within design (requires ``cluster=``, one-way); matches R ``clubSandwich::vcovCR(plm)``. - ``"conley"`` -- Conley spatial HAC on the within design (requires ``conley_lat=/conley_lon=/conley_cutoff=``; Stata ``acreg`` planar distance convention). - ``"wild"`` -- shorthand for ``wild=True`` (requires ``cluster=``).

weights.description: Observation weights. Column name or raw array.

wild.description: If True (and ``cluster`` is given), return wild-cluster-bootstrap p-values / CIs alongside classical cluster SE. Applied variable- by-variable. Only supported with a single cluster column. This is ``boottest``'s WCR bootstrap with the null imposed and the fixed effects **re-absorbed** in every draw (exactly, through ``2G`` sweeps of cluster-indicator columns done once). Running the bootstrap on already-demeaned data -- the quick "FWL" shortcut -- is valid only when every absorbed effect is nested in the cluster; otherwise its bootstrap t distribution is too narrow (see ``panel/_wild_fe.py``; on 1.5 million rows with four FE groups and 100 occupation clusters the shortcut gave p = 0.116 against 0.176). The cost is dominated by those ``2G`` sweeps plus the confidence-set inversion, not by the draws themselves (on a 230,000-row subsample 99, 999 and 9,999 draws took 31, 29 and 35 seconds).

name: hdfe_ols

description: Heckman two-step selection model correcting for sample selection bias. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: Heckman / endogenous-treatment models: joint normality of the selection and outcome errors, and an exclusion restriction -- a variable that shifts selection but not the outcome; without it the model is identified only by functional form. Pre-conditions: A selection or attrition indicator observed for every unit, including those with missing outcomes. Failure modes: No credible exclusion restriction for Heckman selection -> Report bounds (sp.attrition_bounds) or a sensitivity analysis instead of a point estimate that rests on normality. Alternatives: sp.sp.attrition_bounds, sp.sp.rosenbaum_bounds, sp.sp.evalue_rr.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals

cluster.description: method='ml' only: cluster column (vce(cluster c))

method.description: 'twostep' (Heckman 1979 probit + OLS with IMR) or 'ml' (full-information ML, Stata's default heckman)

vce.description: method='ml' only: None/'oim', 'robust' or 'cluster' (e.g. vce='cluster firm'); robust= is an alias

weights.description: method='ml' only: sampling weights [pw=] (imply robust SEs)

z.description: Selection-equation variables (include exclusion restrictions in z but not x)

name: heckman

description: Breusch-Pagan test for heteroskedasticity. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: The fitted model whose result is passed in is correctly specified for the test in question; Wald tests use that fit's variance estimator (robust / clustered if it was), so inference inherits its validity. Pre-conditions: A fitted StatsPAI result object (sp.regress / sp.logit / ...) -- these functions do not take raw data. Failure modes: Heteroskedasticity or RESET rejects -> Refit with robust SEs (vce='hc1' / cluster) and consider polynomial or interaction terms. Alternatives: sp.sp.margins, sp.sp.test, sp.sp.regress.

x.description: Primary running variable, regressor, or feature input for this estimator.

y.description: Outcome variable column name or outcome array.

name: het_test

description: Holm (1979) step-down correction. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: the hypotheses are one pre-registered primary outcome -- there is nothing to adjust. Assumptions: Each input p-value is valid on its own (correct size marginally); Bonferroni / Holm control the family-wise error rate under arbitrary dependence; Benjamini-Hochberg controls the false discovery rate under independence or positive regression dependence. Pre-conditions: The family of hypotheses is fixed before looking at the data; adding tests after the fact invalidates the control. Failure modes: All adjusted p-values become 1 with many hypotheses -> Bonferroni / Holm are very conservative for large families; report FDR (sp.benjamini_hochberg) or Romano-Wolf. Alternatives: sp.sp.romano_wolf, sp.sp.benjamini_hochberg.
name: holm

description: Rambachan-Roth (2023) 'honest' DID sensitivity analysis. Operates on a fitted event-study / DID result: pass ``result_id`` from a prior ``sp.event_study`` / ``sp.callaway_santanna`` / ``sp.did_imputation`` / ``sp.sun_abraham`` fit run with ``as_handle=true`` (or use the ``honest_did_from_result`` tool, which auto-extracts the event-study coefficients). Returns honest confidence intervals under varying degrees of parallel-trends violation (smoothness or relative-magnitude restrictions). Call this when a pre-trend test rejects at low power instead of abandoning the design. Validation: certified parity evidence.

alpha.description: Significance level for the honest CI.

e.description: Event-time period (post-treatment horizon) to build the honest CI for.

m_grid.description: Grid of M bounds on the parallel-trends violation to sweep.

method.description: Restriction family: 'smoothness' (second differences) or 'relative_magnitude'.

name: honest_did

description: Rambachan-Roth sensitivity from a coefficient vector and its covariance. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact).

alpha.description: As in :func:`honest_did`.

betahat.description: Event-study coefficients, the reference period excluded. Or a fitted result with ``params`` and a full covariance (``sp.hdfe_ols``, ``sp.regress``, ``sp.feols`` ...) together with ``event_times`` as a ``{coefficient name: event time}`` mapping: the coefficients and their covariance block are taken from the fit, so a hand-built intensity event study (``exposure x 1[t = k]`` regressors) goes straight in.

event_times.description: Relative time of each coefficient (negative = pre-treatment, ``>= 0`` = post); a ``{name: time}`` dict with a fitted ``betahat``. If omitted, ``num_pre_periods`` must be given and the times are ``-num_pre_periods-1 .. -2`` for the leads (``-1`` is the omitted reference) and ``0, 1, ...`` for the lags -- HonestDiD's layout.

method.description: As in :func:`honest_did`.

num_pre_periods.description: Number of leading pre-treatment coefficients when ``event_times`` is omitted.

sigma.description: Their joint covariance matrix (``len(betahat)`` square). Use the full

name: honest_did_from_moments

description: Rambachan-Roth (2023) honest CIs on a fitted DID / event-study result. Auto-extracts betas + sigma + pre/post-period counts from the result; the LLM never ferries arrays. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact).

method.description: SD = smoothness deviation (Rambachan-Roth default); RM = relative magnitude.

result_id.description: Handle to a DID / event-study result.

name: honest_did_from_result

description: Half-sample spread of the mean CATE prediction (deprecated). Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Assumptions: Unconfoundedness given the covariates; Overlap / positivity; Honesty: separate subsamples are used to choose splits and to estimate effects. Pre-conditions: Covariates, treatment, and outcome with enough data to grow an honest forest. Failure modes: Calibration test rejects -- the forest's heterogeneity is not well calibrated -> Increase the sample / number of trees, or fall back to a doubly-robust learner. Alternatives: sp.dml, sp.auto_cate, sp.tmle. Typical minimum N: 1000.

seed.description: Random seed for reproducible stochastic steps.

name: honest_variance

description: Horowitz-Manski (2000) bounds conditioning on covariates. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: Only weak (set-identifying) assumptions are imposed; the result is an interval, not a point; Lee bounds add monotonicity of selection; Oster's delta adds proportional selection on observed vs. unobserved. Pre-conditions: The data needed for the point-identifying analysis, plus the weakest credible identifying restriction; For Lee bounds: a binary selection/attrition indicator. Failure modes: Bounds are too wide to be informative -> Add a credible auxiliary restriction (monotone treatment response, instrument) to tighten the bounds. Alternatives: sp.oster_delta, sp.lee_bounds, sp.manski_bounds. Typical minimum N: 100.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

covariates.description: Covariates to condition on (discretised via quartiles for continuous variables).

random_state.description: Random seed or RandomState for reproducible stochastic steps.

y_lower.description: Known lower bound of Y. Defaults to observed min.

y_upper.description: Known upper bound of Y. Defaults to observed max.

description: Hurdle (two-part) model for count data. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: the outcome is a rate with a known exposure -- model the count with an exposure offset rather than the ratio. Assumptions: The conditional mean is exp(x'b); Poisson pseudo-ML is consistent for the mean under this alone, but its default SEs assume equidispersion -- use robust / clustered SEs; Zero-inflated and hurdle models assume a separate process generates the excess zeros; they are not a fix for over-dispersion by itself; Observations are independent conditional on covariates or the dependence is declared (cluster= / random effects). Pre-conditions: Outcome is a non-negative integer count (or non-negative real for PPML gravity-type models); For ppmlhdfe: fixed effects that perfectly predict zeros are dropped along with their observations -- check the reported count. Failure modes: Over-dispersion: Poisson deviance / Pearson chi-square far above degrees of freedom -> Switch to negative binomial (sp.nbreg / sp.zinb) or keep Poisson with robust SEs; the mean is still consistently estimated; Separation: a fixed effect or covariate perfectly predicts zero outcomes -> ppmlhdfe drops those...

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

cluster.description: Cluster identifier column for clustered standard errors.

robust.description: Robust standard-error or covariance estimator option.

x.description: Regressors (used for both hurdle and count parts).

name: hurdle

description: Intra-class correlation for a fitted random-intercept model. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: A random-intercept model: group effects are independent of the residual and each has constant variance; the ICC is the group-level share of variance under that model. Pre-conditions: Inputs / outputs per decision-making unit for frontier tools; a fitted effect and baseline risk for NNT. Alternatives: sp.sp.regress, sp.sp.decompose.

alpha.description: Significance level for the confidence interval. Default 0.05.

component.description: Random-intercept name (``"_cons"``); for a three-level fit the grouping column of the level whose ICC is wanted.

n_boot.description: Parametric-bootstrap intervals are not implemented; must be 0.

result.description: A ``MixedResult`` from :func:`statspai.mixed` or an ``MEGLMResult`` from ``melogit`` / ``meologit`` / ``meglm(family='gaussian')``, with a random intercept only.

seed.description: Unused (reserved for the bootstrap).

name: icc

description: Causal Impact visualization (Google-style 3-panel plot).

type.description: 'all': 3-panel (original + pointwise + cumulative). 'original': actual vs counterfactual. 'pointwise': pointwise causal effect. 'cumulative': cumulative effect.

name: impactplot

description: Compute a single inequality index. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: The 'explained' component depends on the reference coefficient vector; sequential (path-dependent) decompositions depend on the ordering unless a Shapley / Gelbach-type invariant is used; Overlapping support of covariates across groups (reweighting / RIF methods are invalid outside overlap); Linearity assumption holds for Oaxaca-Blinder-type decompositions; non-linear methods (FFL/DFL/Machado-Mata) relax this. Pre-conditions: A group indicator with both groups well represented, and the same covariate set fitted in each group; Data contains a binary or categorical group indicator with both groups represented; Outcome and covariates are numeric (or properly encoded) and finite. Failure modes: Trimming warning at common-support boundaries -> Inspect propensity-score support; restrict the analysis sample or use bounds; RIF coefficients explode at distribution tails -> Use higher-bandwidth kernel density, restrict quantile range, or switch to FFL. Alternatives: sp.sp.decompose, sp.sp.oaxaca, sp.sp.gelbach, sp.dfl_decompose. Typical minimum N: 200.

description: Export the per-unit influence functions of a Callaway-Sant'Anna fit as a tidy, self-contained DataFrame (optionally written to disk) -- the StatsPAI equivalent of Stata csdid saverif(). Feed the export to sp.aggte_from_influence for post-hoc custom aggregation without refitting or re-loading the data. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Pre-conditions: result was produced by sp.callaway_santanna; Imputation: every analysis variable present in the imputation model; randomization inference: the assignment design is known. Failure modes: result carries no influence functions -> Fit with sp.callaway_santanna first; other estimators do not store the (g,t) influence-function grid. Alternatives: sp.aggte, sp.aggte_from_influence, sp.sp.mice, sp.sp.ri_test. Typical minimum N: 50.

description: Instrumental forest: heterogeneous local average treatment effects. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Assumptions: Unconfoundedness: Y(d) independent of D given X (pooled forest); Overlap: 0 < P(D=1 | X) < 1 for the estimand support; fe=: conditional parallel trends and no anticipation; treatment varies within units. Pre-conditions: treatment is binary 0/1 (continuous allowed with discrete_treatment=False); covariates are numeric and finite; encode categoricals beforehand; n >= ~1000 for stable CATE -- forests are data-hungry. Failure modes: sp.calibration_test differential_forest_prediction p_one_sided > 0.05 -> No detectable heterogeneity: report the average effect, not the CATE ranking; average_treatment_effect(target_sample='all') raises MethodIncompatibility on an fe= forest -> Parallel trends identifies effects on treated cells: use target_sample='treated' (imputation ATT) or sp.forest_group_effects; counterfactual effects of never-treated units are extrapolations (sp.forest_support); Panel data fitted without clusters= (units repeat across rows) -> Refit with clusters=unit; i.i.d. honesty and SEs are inva...

W_hat.description: Precomputed ``E[Y|X]``, ``E[W|X]``, ``E[Z|X]``; by default each is the out-of-bag prediction of a regression forest with ``max(50, n_estimators // 4)`` trees.

Y_hat.description: Precomputed ``E[Y|X]``, ``E[W|X]``, ``E[Z|X]``; by default each is the out-of-bag prediction of a regression forest with ``max(50, n_estimators // 4)`` trees.

Z_hat.description: Precomputed ``E[Y|X]``, ``E[W|X]``, ``E[Z|X]``; by default each is the out-of-bag prediction of a regression forest with ``max(50, n_estimators // 4)`` trees.

alpha.description: Significance level of the reported interval.

ci_group_size.description: Trees per little bag; 1 disables variance estimates.

clusters.description: Cluster ids: trees sample whole clusters and every standard error is cluster-robust.

compliance_score.description: ``Delta(X_i)`` for the average-effect scores; by default estimated by an auxiliary 500-tree causal forest of ``W`` on ``Z``.

covariates.description: Effect modifiers ``X``; the nuisances are also regressed on them.

equalize_cluster_weights.description: Give every cluster the same weight (incompatible with ``weights``).

instrument.description: Outcome, treatment (binary or continuous) and instrument (binary or continuous).

max_samples.description: Fraction of clusters drawn per tree (grf ``sample.fraction``).

mtry.description: Candidate variables per split (grf default ``min(ceil(sqrt(p) + 20), p)``).

n_bootstrap.description: Ignored. Standard errors now come from the doubly-robust scores.

random_state.description: Random seed or RandomState for reproducible stochastic steps.

reduced_form_weight.description: Mix the IV split criterion with the causal-forest criterion that treats ``W`` as exogenous (grf ``reduced.form.weight``).

split_alpha.description: grf ``alpha``: minimum share of the parent's instrument variation each child of a stabilised split keeps.

stabilize_splits.description: Use the instrument in the split constraints.

treat.description: Outcome, treatment (binary or continuous) and instrument (binary or continuous).

y.description: Outcome, treatment (binary or continuous) and instrument (binary or continuous).

name: instrumental_forest

description: Interactive fixed effects estimator (Bai 2009). Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: T is large relative to N -- the Nickell bias that motivates GMM is O(1/T) and within estimation is fine. Assumptions: Interactive fixed effects: the factor structure has a small, known number of factors; Static FE: strict exogeneity of regressors conditional on unit fixed effects (E[u_it | x_i, alpha_i] = 0); Random effects: unit effect uncorrelated with regressors; relax with Mundlak / Chamberlain. Pre-conditions: A panel with T >= 3 (T >= 4 for AR(2) testing) and unit / time identifiers; Data is a long-format panel keyed by (entity, time) with at least 2 time periods per entity; Outcome and regressors are numeric or properly encoded. Failure modes: Hausman test rejects RE -> Switch to fixed effects (method='fe') or correlated random effects (method='mundlak'); Few clusters (< 30) inflate Type I error with cluster-robust SEs -> Use wild-cluster bootstrap or CR2/CR3 small-sample corrections; High-dimensional fixed effects make the design singular -> Switch to method='hdfe' / feols for absorption, or drop singletons. Alternatives: sp.sp.xtlsdvc, sp.sp.panel, sp.feols, sp.hdfe_ols...

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

dof.description: Parameters absorbed by the factor structure. ``'exact'`` counts ``r(N + T - r)`` (``F'`` is identified only up to an rxr rotation); ``'regife'`` counts ``r(N + T)``, as Stata ``regife`` does through ``reghdfe`` (which flags that it could not detect the redundant ones). Enters ``sigma2`` and ``K`` in the cluster factor.

method.description: Bai's (2009) iterated least squares: alternate principal components of ``Y - Xbeta`` (factors) and least squares of ``Y M_F`` on ``X M_F`` (slopes) until the slopes move by less than ``tol``. ``'pca'`` is accepted for backward compatibility and runs the same algorithm (it always did); it is deprecated.

robust.description: ``True``: cluster-robust by unit (Bai's ``D0-1 D_Z D0-1`` with the Stata CR1 factor ``G/(G-1)*(NT-1)/(NT-K)``); ``False``: Bai's homoskedastic ``sigma2 D0-1``. In both, the regressors enter through ``Z_j = M_ X_j M_F`` -- projected off *both* the factor space and the loading space.

tol.description: Convergence criterion on max |Deltabeta|. The iteration converges linearly, so the default is tight (``regife``'s own default is 1e-9).

name: interactive_fe

description: Unified interference / spillover dispatcher. design= selects the estimator: 'partial' (Hudgens-Halloran cluster) / 'network_exposure' (Aronow-Samii HT) / 'peer_effects' (Manski / Bramoulle linear-in-means) / 'network_hte' (Wu & Yuan 2025 orthogonal, arXiv:2509.18484) / 'inward_outward' (directed network; Fang, Airoldi & Forastiere 2025, arXiv:2506.06615) / 'cluster_matched_pair' (Bai 2022) / 'cluster_cross' (Ding et al. 2025) / 'cluster_staggered' (Zhou et al. 2025) / 'dnc_gnn' (Zhao et al. 2026). Kwargs pass through to the target function; see sp.interference_family guide. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Assumptions: Partial interference (within-cluster spillover only) OR an explicit exposure mapping; SUTVA modulo the declared spillover structure; Correctly specified exposure function (e.g. fraction-treated, neighbour-share). Pre-conditions: clustered data OR network / adjacency matrix; treatment varies within cluster (or exposure is well-defined on the network); enough clusters (>= 30) for cluster-robust inference. Failure modes: Few clusters (< 30) with cluster-level inference -> Use wild cluster bootstrap...

design.description: Interference design -- call sp.interference_available_designs() for the full list.

name: interference

description: Conditional marginal effects of ``d`` across a moderator ``x`` Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: Treatment is unconfounded given the covariates at every value of the moderator; The linear estimator assumes the marginal effect is linear in the moderator; the binning and kernel estimators relax that and are the check on it; Common support: every treatment level is observed across the range of the moderator over which effects are reported. Pre-conditions: Long (person-period) data with time-varying treatment and covariates in temporal order; a clear time zero for target-trial emulation. Failure modes: The moderator has sparse support in part of its range: marginal effects there are extrapolation -> Use the binning or kernel estimator and show the moderator histogram under the plot. Alternatives: sp.sp.gformula_mc, sp.sp.target_trial_emulate, sp.sp.msm.

adaptive.description: Kernel estimator only. ``True`` scales the bandwidth at each evaluation point by the moderator's density as the R package does (``h(x) = bw * sqrt(geometric-mean density / density(x))``); ``False`` uses the fixed Gaussian kernel ``phi((X - x)/bw)`` of the Stata ``interflex`` command.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

bw.description: Kernel bandwidth on the moderator's scale (before the adaptive density scaling). ``estimator='kernel'`` needs either ``bw`` or ``cv=True``, which selects it by interflex's cross-validation (``interflex(bw = NULL)``).

bw_grid.description: interflex ``grid``: an integer gives that many candidates log-spaced from ``range(x)/100`` to ``range(x)``; a sequence is used as the grid.

cv.description: Kernel estimator only: choose ``bw`` by interflex's k-fold cross-validation. Observations are split into ``kfold`` folds stratified on ``d`` (``interflex:::createFolds``); for every candidate bandwidth the local-linear coefficients are fitted on the training folds over the evaluation grid (with the training sample's moderator density for the adaptive scaling), carried to each test observation by linear interpolation between its two nearest grid points, and the mean squared (``metric='mse'``) or absolute (``'mae'``) prediction error of ``y`` is averaged over folds; the bandwidth minimising it, divided by the number of evaluation points that produced a fit, is chosen exactly as the R package does. Requires ``bw=None``.

d.description: Outcome, treatment (binary 0/1 or continuous) and moderator.

nbins.description: Number of moderator bins (cut at sample quantiles) for the binning estimator; ``cutoffs`` overrides the quantiles.

neval.description: Evaluation points, equally spaced over the moderator's range.

random_state.description: Seed for the fold assignment. interflex draws its folds with R's stream, so the selection is compared to R statistically (across seeds), not byte for byte.

seed.description: Bootstrap replications and seed.

treat_type.description: Inferred from ``d`` when omitted (two distinct values = discrete).

vce.description: Variance construction. ``'robust'`` is the HC1 sandwich (interflex's default) and ``'homoscedastic'`` the classical covariance for the linear and binning models and the Wald test; ``'bootstrap'`` (kernel estimator only) draws nonparametric bootstrap standard errors, the linear and binning estimators always reporting delta-method SEs.

wald.description: Report the Wald and LR tests of the linear interaction against the binning model (``estimator='binning'`` or ``'linear'``).

wald_full_moderate.description: Whether the fully interacted model behind the Wald / LR tests also interacts the covariates ``z`` with the bins (R interflex). The Stata command leaves the covariates uninteracted; set ``False`` to reproduce its test.

wald_test.description: Reference distribution of the Wald statistic: chi-square (R ``lmtest::waldtest(test = "Chisq")``) or the F distribution with the full model's residual degrees of freedom (Stata interflex).

x.description: Outcome, treatment (binary 0/1 or continuous) and moderator.

y.description: Outcome, treatment (binary 0/1 or continuous) and moderator.

name: interflex

description: The interflex figure: marginal effect of ``d`` across ``x`` with its

ax.description: Draw into an existing axes; a new figure is created otherwise.

show_hist.description: Add the moderator histogram (treated / control) under the curve.

name: interflex_plot

description: Natural-language interpretation of a fitted result. When the connected MCP client advertised sampling, this REUSES the agent's own model (no API key) to explain the estimate, its uncertainty, and what the design does / does not identify -- optionally focused by a `question` and tuned for an `audience`. With no sampling available it falls back to a deterministic structured brief: it NEVER fabricates a narrative. Every claim is grounded in the result's own numbers -- the model is told not to invent estimates. Pass the result_id from an earlier as_handle=true call.

audience.description: Tone / depth: 'researcher' (precise, names identification assumptions), 'policymaker' (plain, decision-focused), 'general' (no jargon).

question.description: Optional specific question to focus the interpretation (e.g. 'is the effect economically meaningful?').

name: interpret_result

description: Inverse propensity score OPE. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: Logging (behaviour) policy propensities are known or correctly estimated; Positivity / common support: the logging policy assigns positive probability to every action the target policy takes; No unmeasured confounding in the logged data. Pre-conditions: X (context), A (logged action), R (reward) and logging propensities are available. Failure modes: High-variance estimate from extreme importance weights when the target policy diverges from logging -> Use self-normalised IPS (snips) or the doubly-robust estimator to reduce variance. Alternatives: sp.snips, sp.doubly_robust, sp.direct_method. Typical minimum N: 500.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

name: ips

description: Inverse Probability Weighting for ATE/ATT/ATC with propensity score trimming. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: The propensity model is correctly specified: IPW has no outcome model to fall back on (sp.aipw is doubly robust); Unconfoundedness: no unmeasured confounding of the point treatment given the covariates; Positivity / overlap: 0 < P(D=1 | X) < 1 on the estimand's support. Pre-conditions: Sequentially measured covariates, (time-varying) treatment, and outcome; Models for the treatment process and the outcome (or weights). Failure modes: Stabilized weights have extreme values (positivity near-violation) -> Truncate weights, simplify the treatment model, or use a doubly-robust estimator (TMLE). Alternatives: sp.tmle, sp.g_computation. Typical minimum N: 300.

cluster.description: Cluster column: cluster bootstrap, or cluster-summed sandwich with se_method='sandwich'

covariates.description: Variables for the propensity score model (logistic regression).

ps_model.description: Propensity-score model; 'probit' is teffects ipw (..., probit)

se_method.description: 'sandwich' = teffects ipw robust M-estimation SE (needs normalize=True, trim=0)

weights.description: Sampling-weight column (Stata [pw=]); weights the logit and multiplies each IPW weight

name: ipw

description: Compute impulse response functions from VAR. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: the question is a treatment effect with a control series available -- sp.causal_impact / sp.synth use the control to absorb common shocks that a single-series ITS attributes to the intervention. Assumptions: Stationarity after the chosen differencing (ARIMA, VAR, Granger); unit-root series need cointegration analysis (Engle-Granger, Johansen), not levels regressions; Impulse responses depend on the identification scheme (Cholesky ordering, sign restrictions); interrupted time series assumes no concurrent shock at the intervention date. Pre-conditions: A regularly spaced time index without gaps; enough observations per parameter (rule of thumb: >= 50 for ARIMA, more for VAR / GARCH). Failure modes: Unit root detected in a series used in levels -> Difference the series or test for cointegration (sp.engle_granger / sp.johansen) before modelling. Alternatives: sp.sp.arima, sp.sp.its, sp.sp.causal_impact.

sigma_df.description: Divisor of the residual covariance that the orthogonalisation uses: ``'ml'`` = ``T`` (Stata ``irf create`` after ``var``), ``'unbiased'`` = ``T - m`` with ``m`` regressors per equation (``vars::Psi``, and Stata after ``var, dfk``). Default follows the fitted model's ``se_df`` (``'stata'``/``'ml'`` -> ``'ml'``, ``'r'``/``'unbiased'`` -> ``'unbiased'``). Irrelevant when ``orthogonal=False``.

name: irf

description: Segmented regression for interrupted time series. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: the question is a treatment effect with a control series available -- sp.causal_impact / sp.synth use the control to absorb common shocks that a single-series ITS attributes to the intervention. Assumptions: Stationarity after the chosen differencing (ARIMA, VAR, Granger); unit-root series need cointegration analysis (Engle-Granger, Johansen), not levels regressions; Impulse responses depend on the identification scheme (Cholesky ordering, sign restrictions); interrupted time series assumes no concurrent shock at the intervention date. Pre-conditions: A regularly spaced time index without gaps; enough observations per parameter (rule of thumb: >= 50 for ARIMA, more for VAR / GARCH). Failure modes: Unit root detected in a series used in levels -> Difference the series or test for cointegration (sp.engle_granger / sp.johansen) before modelling. Alternatives: sp.sp.arima, sp.sp.causal_impact.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

intervention.description: Time index (integer row position) at which the intervention begins. Required.

seasonality_period.description: Period P of Fourier seasonal terms (e.g. 12 for monthly data with annual cycle). If None, no seasonality is added.

time.description: Time column. If None, uses row index 0..n-1.

name: its

description: Unified IV estimation and the entry point for the whole IV family: k-class (2SLS, LIML, Fuller, GMM, JIVE) plus the many-weak-instrument jackknife variants (jive1, ujive, ijive, rjive, jive_mw), rigorous/post-Lasso instrument selection (lasso, rlasso, post_lasso), marginal treatment effects (mte) and their MST sharp bounds (ivmte_bounds), plausibly-exogenous sensitivity (plausibly_exog_ltz / plausibly_exog_uci), nonparametric and ML variants (npiv, kernel, ivdml, deepiv), quantile IV (ivqreg), Bayesian IV (bayes), continuous-instrument LATE (continuous_late), many-weak-IV Anderson-Rubin (many_weak_ar) and shift-share (shift_share). Includes first-stage F, Sargan/Hansen J, Kleibergen-Paap rk, Sanderson-Windmeijer per-endog F and Hausman diagnostics. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: the instrument is a policy cutoff on a running variable -- that is a fuzzy RD (sp.rdrobust(..., fuzzy=)), whose local inference differs. Cost: augmented_diagnostics=True adds bootstrap SEs and AR / CLR grid inversions; cost is n_boot + grid_size extra fits. Assumptions: Relevance: instruments predict the endogenous regressor (first-stage F >= 10 rule of thumb); Exclusion: instrumen...

augmented_diagnostics.description: When the method returns EconometricResults, attach the Kleibergen-Paap rk statistic, Sanderson-Windmeijer per-endogenous F and Olea-Pflueger effective F to result.diagnostics.

cluster.description: Column name for cluster-robust SEs

method.description: Estimation method. The k-class methods (2sls, liml, fuller, gmm, jive) take `formula` + `data`; the rest take their own explicit arguments -- see the target function's docstring. Aliases are case-insensitive and -/_ interchangeable.

robust.description: Standard error type

small.description: Small-sample statistics as Stata ivregress, small (N-K divisor, HC1, G/(G-1)(N-1)/(N-K) cluster factor, t/F); False gives ivregress' default large-sample statistics (N divisor, HC0, no cluster factor, z/chi2). 2SLS/LIML

name: iv

description: Nevo-Rosen (2012) bounds for LATE under imperfect instruments. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Assumptions: Only weak (set-identifying) assumptions are imposed; the result is an interval, not a point; Lee bounds add monotonicity of selection; Oster's delta adds proportional selection on observed vs. unobserved. Pre-conditions: The data needed for the point-identifying analysis, plus the weakest credible identifying restriction; For Lee bounds: a binary selection/attrition indicator. Failure modes: Bounds are too wide to be informative -> Add a credible auxiliary restriction (monotone treatment response, instrument) to tighten the bounds. Alternatives: sp.oster_delta, sp.lee_bounds, sp.manski_bounds. Typical minimum N: 100.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals and tests.

assumption.description: - ``'monotone_iv'``: instrument has same-sign direct effect as through the treatment (Nevo-Rosen Proposition 2). - ``'less_than_late'``: direct effect of Z on Y is weakly less than the indirect effect (tighter).

random_state.description: Random seed or RandomState for reproducible stochastic steps.

name: iv_bounds

description: Run several k-class / JIVE estimators on the same IV specification and return a one-row-per-method comparison DataFrame (estimate, SE, CI, first-stage F). Useful as a sensitivity sanity check before reporting. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Assumptions: Instrument relevance (non-zero first stage); Exclusion restriction: the instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment; Independence/exogeneity of the instrument; for LATE, monotonicity (no defiers). Pre-conditions: An instrument plausibly affecting treatment, an endogenous treatment, and an outcome; A strong first stage (assess instrument strength before interpreting estimates). Failure modes: Weak first stage -- biased point estimates and unreliable conventional SEs -> Report first-stage F / effective F and use weak-IV-robust inference (Anderson-Rubin). Alternatives: sp.iv, sp.anderson_rubin_ci, sp.dml. Typical minimum N: 200.

alpha.description: For Wald-CI columns.

methods.description: Methods to dispatch through :func:`sp.iv` (and therefore the unified IV dispatcher).

name: iv_compare

description: Modern IV reporting bundle (R `ivDiag` analogue). Combines 2SLS point estimate, analytic + pairs/wild bootstrap SEs, Olea-Pflueger effective F, Lee-McCrary-Moreira-Porter (2022) tF-corrected critical value, Anderson-Rubin / CLR / K weak-IV-robust confidence sets, Kleibergen-Paap rk LM, Conley-Hansen-Rossi (2012) plausibly-exogenous LTZ sensitivity, and a Blandhol-Bonney-Mogstad-Torgovitsky (2022/2025) / Soczynski (2024) `TSLS-as-LATE` caveat into a single IVDiagResult. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: a quick point estimate is all that is needed -- this is the full reporting bundle (bootstrap SEs, tF, AR / CLR / K sets, LTZ) and costs many fits. Cost: n_boot bootstrap fits plus grid_size test inversions per confidence set; minutes on n ~ 10^5. Assumptions: Instrument relevance (non-zero first stage); Exclusion restriction: the instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment; Independence/exogeneity of the instrument; for LATE, monotonicity (no defiers). Pre-conditions: An instrument plausibly affecting treatment, an endogenous treatment, and an outcome; A strong first stage (assess instrument strength before interpreting estimates). Failure modes:...

absorb.description: High-dimensional fixed effects to partial out before the bundle is computed, so every statistic describes the absorbed specification (ivreghdfe-equivalent)

alpha.description: Significance level for all CIs.

cluster.description: Cluster column for cluster-robust SE / cluster bootstrap

include_clr_ci.description: Optionally invert CLR / K tests on a grid for the matching confidence set (slower; CLR critical values are the exact conditional quantiles).

include_k_ci.description: Optionally invert CLR / K tests on a grid for the matching confidence set (slower; CLR critical values are the exact conditional quantiles).

ltz_gamma_sd.description: Standard deviation of CHR (2012) LTZ Gaussian prior on gamma

random_state.description: Seed for bootstrap and CLR Monte-Carlo.

name: iv_diag

description: Instrumental forest (grf::instrumental_forest): heterogeneous local average treatment effects tau(x) = Cov[Y,Z|x]/Cov[W,Z|x] from an honest generalized random forest that splits on the IV gradient and uses the instrument in its split constraints. Reports out-of-bag CATEs with little-bag variances and the doubly-robust average conditional LATE (compliance-weighted scores). Given grf's forest, the local solve, scores, average and BLP match grf to 1e-13 (T2); the forest itself is checked only statistically (a stochastic screen against grf on known-truth designs, not a seed-replicated equivalence test). Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Assumptions: instrument relevance, exclusion and independence given X; monotonicity for a complier interpretation of tau(x). Pre-conditions: instrument varies within covariate cells; first stage not near zero anywhere. Failure modes: DataInsufficient: the instrument has no variation -> Use a varying instrument; UserWarning: compliance score near zero -> Locally weak instrument; trim covariate regions or report the ATE with caution. Alternatives: sp.ivreg, sp.dml, sp.causal_forest. Ty...

W_hat.description: Precomputed E[W|X]; default out-of-bag regression forest.

Y_hat.description: Precomputed E[Y|X]; default out-of-bag regression forest.

Z_hat.description: Precomputed E[Z|X]; default out-of-bag regression forest.

alpha.description: Significance level of the reported interval.

ci_group_size.description: Trees per little bag; 1 disables variance estimates.

clusters.description: Cluster ids: trees sample whole clusters and every standard error is cluster-robust.

compliance_score.description: ``Delta(X_i)`` for the average-effect scores; by default estimated by an auxiliary 500-tree causal forest of ``W`` on ``Z``.

covariates.description: Effect modifiers ``X``; the nuisances are also regressed on them.

equalize_cluster_weights.description: Give every cluster the same weight (incompatible with ``weights``).

honest.description: grf honesty: grow on one half of the drawn sample, estimate leaves on the other.

honesty_fraction.description: Share of the drawn sample used to grow the tree.

honesty_prune_leaves.description: Prune leaves left empty by the estimation half.

max_samples.description: Fraction of clusters drawn per tree (grf ``sample.fraction``).

mtry.description: Candidate variables per split (grf default ``min(ceil(sqrt(p) + 20), p)``).

n_bootstrap.description: Ignored. Standard errors now come from the doubly-robust scores.

n_jobs.description: Threads used to grow trees (-1 = all cores).

random_state.description: Seed; different seeds give independent forests.

reduced_form_weight.description: Mix the IV split criterion with the causal-forest criterion that treats ``W`` as exogenous (grf ``reduced.form.weight``).

split_alpha.description: grf ``alpha``: minimum share of the parent's instrument variation each child of a stabilised split keeps.

stabilize_splits.description: Use the instrument in the split constraints.

name: iv_forest

description: Exponential-mean (Poisson) regression with endogenous regressors by GMM, additive or multiplicative errors, as Stata's ivpoisson gmm. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: Endogeneity comes from an omitted variable inside the exponential and errors='additive' is kept: that moment condition is not valid there; use errors='multiplicative'. Assumptions: Conditional mean is exp(x'b); Instruments are uncorrelated with the additive (or multiplicative) error and relevant. Pre-conditions: Outcome is non-negative; At least as many excluded instruments as endogenous regressors. Failure modes: GMM criterion did not converge -> Rescale regressors on a very large scale; try errors='additive'. Alternatives: sp.poisson, sp.ppmlhdfe, sp.ivreg. Typical minimum N: 200.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals

cluster.description: Cluster column (vce(cluster c))

errors.description: Moment condition: 'additive' E[z(y - exp(xb))] = 0 or 'multiplicative' E[z(y/exp(xb) - 1)] = 0 (Mullahy 1997)

instruments.description: Excluded instruments, at least as many as endog

maxiter.description: Maximum Gauss-Newton iterations per GMM step

method.description: GMM weighting: 'onestep', 'twostep' or 'igmm' (iterated)

tol.description: Convergence tolerance on the parameter step

vce.description: Moment covariance: 'robust', 'cluster' or 'unadjusted'

wmatrix.description: Weight-matrix covariance when it should differ from vce

x.description: Exogenous regressors of the outcome equation

name: ivpoisson

description: Probit with continuous endogenous regressors: maximum likelihood or Newey's two-step, as Stata's ivprobit. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: The endogenous regressor is binary: the linear normal reduced form is wrong; use sp.biprobit; Comparing magnitudes across method='mle' and method='twostep': the two use different scale normalisations. Assumptions: Outcome error and reduced-form errors are jointly normal; Instruments are excluded from the outcome equation and relevant for every endogenous regressor; Endogenous regressors are continuous with a linear reduced form. Pre-conditions: Outcome is binary 0/1 with both values present; At least as many excluded instruments as endogenous regressors. Failure modes: rank condition fails / instruments collinear -> Drop redundant instruments or add one that moves the endogenous regressor. Alternatives: sp.biprobit, sp.ivreg, sp.probit. Typical minimum N: 200.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals

cluster.description: Cluster column (vce(cluster c))

instruments.description: Excluded instruments, at least as many as endog

method.description: 'mle' (joint maximum likelihood) or 'twostep' (Newey's minimum chi-squared)

vce.description: method='mle' only: None/'oim', 'robust' or 'cluster' (e.g. vce='cluster firm'); robust= is an alias

x.description: Exogenous regressors of the outcome equation

name: ivprobit

description: Instrumental-variable quantile regression (Chernozhukov-Hansen). Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Do NOT use when: the object of interest is a treatment effect and covariates were chosen by stepwise selection -- use sp.dml, which handles selection with valid inference. Assumptions: Quantile IV (ivqreg): rank invariance / monotonicity of the structural quantile function; Conditional mean independence: E[u|X] = 0; No perfect collinearity. Pre-conditions: A model formula (or equation list for systems) and a data frame; high-dimensional fixed effects go through absorb= / sp.feols; data is a pandas DataFrame with every variable in formula as a column; outcome is numeric; non-numeric regressors should be categorical (handled via patsy). Failure modes: Singular design / LinAlgError -> Drop collinear regressors or check dummy-variable coding; Heteroskedasticity test rejects (sp.het_test) -> Re-estimate with robust='hc1' (or 'hc3' for n < 250); Few clusters (< 30) with cluster-robust SEs -> Use wild cluster bootstrap (sp.wild_cluster_bootstrap) or CR3 adjustment. Alternatives: sp.sp.regress, sp.sp.feols, sp.sp.iv, sp.iv...

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals.

bootstrap.description: Number of pairs-bootstrap replications for standard errors. ``0`` disables bootstrap; asymptotic rank-test inversion is not implemented in this MVP.

instruments.description: Instrument(s) ``Z``. Must be at least as many as ``endog``.

n_grid.description: Grid resolution for the profile search over ``alpha`` (scalar case) -- ignored when ``endog`` is multi-dimensional.

random_state.description: Random seed or RandomState for reproducible stochastic steps.

refine.description: After the grid search, refine ``alpha`` with a local optimizer.

name: ivqreg

description: 2SLS instrumental-variables regression with robust or clustered SEs and first-stage F diagnostics. Formula syntax: 'y ~ x_exog + (d_endog ~ z_instrument)'. Validation: certified parity evidence.
name: ivreg

description: Tobit with continuous endogenous regressors: maximum likelihood or Newey's two-step, as Stata's ivtobit. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: Outcome error and reduced-form errors are jointly normal and homoskedastic; Instruments are excluded from the outcome equation and relevant for every endogenous regressor; Censoring limits are known. Pre-conditions: At least one of ll / ul is set; At least as many excluded instruments as endogenous regressors. Failure modes: not enough uncensored observations -> Check the censoring limits; with nearly all observations at the limit the model is a probit. Alternatives: sp.tobit, sp.ivreg, sp.ivprobit. Typical minimum N: 200.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals

cluster.description: Cluster column (vce(cluster c))

instruments.description: Excluded instruments, at least as many as endog

method.description: 'mle' (joint maximum likelihood) or 'twostep' (Newey's minimum chi-squared)

vce.description: method='mle' only: None/'oim', 'robust' or 'cluster' (e.g. vce='cluster firm'); robust= is an alias

x.description: Exogenous regressors of the outcome equation

name: ivtobit

description: Leave-one-cluster-out jackknife standard errors. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: dependence is spatial rather than by group -- use sp.conley with a distance cutoff. Assumptions: Errors are independent across clusters; any within-cluster dependence is unrestricted; Clusters are defined at (or above) the level at which treatment was assigned; Asymptotics run in the number of clusters: the default CR1 sandwich over-rejects with few (< ~30-50) or very unbalanced clusters; CR2 / CR3 / wild cluster bootstrap are the small-G repairs. Pre-conditions: A fitted regression result (or its design matrix and residuals) and a cluster column with no missing values; Two-way clustering needs both dimensions to have many clusters. Failure modes: Few clusters (G < 30) or one dominant cluster -> Report wild cluster bootstrap p-values / inverted CIs (sp.wild_cluster_boot, sp.wild_cluster_ci_inv) or CR3 jackknife; Very few treated clusters -> Cluster-robust SEs are unreliable; use sp.did_few_treated or randomization inference. Alternatives: sp.sp.wild_cluster_boot, sp.sp.cr2_se, sp.sp.conley.

alpha.description: Significance level for confidence intervals.

cluster.description: Name of the cluster variable in ``data``.

name: jackknife_se

description: Jackknife Instrumental Variables Estimation (JIVE). Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: the instrument set is small -- JIVE corrects many-instrument bias and is less efficient than 2SLS with one or two strong instruments. Assumptions: Instrument exogeneity and the exclusion restriction hold; these tools repair inference under weak identification, not invalidity; Relevance: instruments predict the endogenous regressor (first-stage F >= 10 rule of thumb); Exclusion: instruments affect outcome only through the endogenous regressor. Pre-conditions: A fitted IV result (or y, d, z arrays) with the same variance estimator (homoskedastic / robust / clustered) used throughout; formula includes the (endog ~ instruments) parenthesised block; at least as many instruments as endogenous regressors (order condition). name: jive

description: Johansen (1991) cointegration test. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: the question is a treatment effect with a control series available -- sp.causal_impact / sp.synth use the control to absorb common shocks that a single-series ITS attributes to the intervention. Assumptions: Stationarity after the chosen differencing (ARIMA, VAR, Granger); unit-root series need cointegration analysis (Engle-Granger, Johansen), not levels regressions. Pre-conditions: A regularly spaced time index without gaps; enough observations per parameter (rule of thumb: >= 50 for ARIMA, more for VAR / GARCH). Failure modes: Series are not all integrated of order one, or the deterministic terms or lag length are wrong: the cointegration conclusion changes with the specification -> Test the order of integration of each series first and report the result across lag and trend choices. Alternatives: sp.sp.arima, sp.sp.its, sp.sp.causal_impact.

Stata's long names are accepted as aliases.

description: Kaplan-Meier non-parametric survival function estimator. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: competing events are common and the estimand is the probability of the event of interest -- Kaplan-Meier treating them as censored overstates it; use sp.cuminc / sp.finegray. Assumptions: Non-informative (independent) censoring conditional on covariates. Pre-conditions: One duration column (> 0) and one event indicator (1 = event, 0 = censored) per subject; competing risks need an event-type code; Time-varying covariates need a (start, stop] counting-process layout. Failure modes: Few subjects at risk in the right tail: the last steps of the curve rest on a handful of observations -> Report the number at risk under the curve and stop the plotted range where it is small; Competing events treated as censoring: 1 - KM overstates the cumulative incidence of the event of interest -> Estimate the cumulative incidence function with the Aalen-Johansen estimator. Assumptions: Instrument relevance (non-zero first stage); Exclusion restriction: the instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment; Independence/exogeneity of the instrument; for LATE, monotonicity (no defiers). Pre-conditions: An instrument plausibly affecting treatment, an endogenous treatment, and an outcome; A strong first stage (assess instrument strength before interpreting estimates); formula includes the (endog ~ instruments) parenthesised block. Assumptions: The counterfactual density would be smooth through the threshold absent the policy; Excess mass at the threshold reflects the behavioural elasticity of interest; No other discontinuity coincides with the threshold. Pre-conditions: A behavioural choice variable (earnings, hours, ...) with a known kink or notch in the budget/choice set; A visible empirical density of the running variable around the threshold. Failure modes: Round-number heaping or a coincident policy contaminates the bunching mass -> Exclude heaping points, widen the excluded region, and test the counterfactual polynomial order. Alternatives: sp.rdrobust, sp.rkd. Typical minimum N: 500.

description: Kitagawa (1955) two-factor rate decomposition. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: The 'explained' component depends on the reference coefficient vector; sequential (path-dependent) decompositions depend on the ordering unless a Shapley / Gelbach-type invariant is used; Overlapping support of covariates across groups (reweighting / RIF methods are invalid outside overlap); Linearity assumption holds for Oaxaca-Blinder-type decompositions; non-linear methods (FFL/DFL/Machado-Mata) relax this. Pre-conditions: A group indicator with both groups well represented, and the same covariate set fitted in each group; Data contains a binary or categorical group indicator with both groups represented; Outcome and covariates are numeric (or properly encoded) and finite. Failure modes: Explained share changes sign when the reference group is switched -> Report both references or the pooled / Shapley-invariant decomposition; the index-number problem is real, not a bug; Trimming warning at common-support boundaries -> Inspect propensity-score support; restrict the analysis sample or use bounds; RIF coefficients explode at distribution tails -> Use higher-bandwidth kernel density,...

description: Kitagawa (2015) specification test for the validity of LATE. Validation: validated evidence tier (known-truth, reference, external-parity, or Monte Carlo artifact). Do NOT use when: the treatment or instrument is multi-valued or continuous -- the test is defined for the binary instrument / binary treatment design. Cost: n_boot bootstrap replications (default 1000), each re-evaluating the CDF conditions on n_grid points. Assumptions: Tests the joint LATE conditions (instrument independence, exclusion, monotonicity) through their testable implication: the implied complier potential-outcome distributions must be proper CDFs; A non-rejection is not evidence that the LATE assumptions hold; the test only has power against violations that bend the complier CDFs. Pre-conditions: Binary (0/1) instrument and binary (0/1) treatment columns; A first stage that is not essentially zero. Failure modes: Instrument or treatment is not coded 0/1 -> Recode to a binary instrument and a binary treatment; the test is defined for the binary LATE design only; First stage is essentially zero -> The instrument does not move the treatment, so there are no compliers to test; check the first stage before anyt...

Assumptions: Stepwise / lasso selection: post-selection inference on the selected model is invalid without sample splitting or debiasing -- treat them as screening tools; Conditional mean independence: E[u|X] = 0; No perfect collinearity. description: Compute Lee (2009) bounds for ATE under sample selection. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: Only weak (set-identifying) assumptions are imposed; the result is an interval, not a point; Lee bounds add monotonicity of selection; Oster's delta adds proportional selection on observed vs. unobserved. description: Limited Information Maximum Likelihood (LIML) estimator. Validation: certified parity evidence. Do NOT use when: the instruments are strong (effective F far above 10) -- 2SLS is more precise and LIML buys nothing. Assumptions: Relevance: instruments predict the endogenous regressor (first-stage F >= 10 rule of thumb); Exclusion: instruments affect outcome only through the endogenous regressor; Monotonicity (for LATE interpretation under heterogeneous effects). Pre-conditions: At least as many instruments as endogenous regressors; formula includes the (endog ~ instruments) parenthesised block; at least as many instruments as endogenous regressors (order condition). Failure modes: LIML estimate has a much larger SE than 2SLS -> LIML has no finite moments under weak identification; the Fuller modification (fuller=1) restores them; kappa reported as 1.0 (LIML fell back to 2SLS) -> The eigenvalue problem was degenerate (collinear instruments); check the instrument set; First-stage F < 10 (Stock-Yogo 5% bias) -> Use weak-IV-robust inference (Anderson-Rubin) or LIML. Assumptions: The fitted model whose result is passed in is correctly specified for the test in question; Wald tests use that fit's variance estimator (robust / clustered if it was), so inference inherits its validity. Alternatives: sp.pc_algorithm, sp.fci, sp.ges. Typical minimum N: 500.

description: Estimate impulse responses via Jorda (2005) local projections. Validation: certified parity evidence. Assumptions: Outcome and shock series are (covariance-)stationary so horizon-h projections are not spurious; Shock is conditionally exogenous at t given controls and the auto-added lags (no contemporaneous feedback from y_t to shock_t); Newey-West truncation lag is adequate for the moving-average serial correlation induced by overlapping horizons. auto_lag.description: If ``True`` (the legacy default), also adds ``y_{t-1}`` and ``shock_{t-1}`` as automatic regressors. Set ``False`` for a bare ``y_{t+h} ~ const + shock_t + controls`` specification. These two auto-controls were silent in the pre-1.16 docstring.

controls.description: Additional regressors taken **verbatim** from ``data``: the column values at time t are used directly, without re-lagging. If you want the lag of a control, lag it yourself before passing it in (e.g. ``df["unemp_lag"] = df["unemp"].shift(1)`` and then ``controls=["unemp_lag"]``). The pre-1.16 behaviour silently re-lagged controls a second time on top of an auto- added ``y_{t-1}``, producing collinear columns and surprising impulse responses; see ``MIGRATION.md`` for context.
